chunks: And Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who enters into a salam contract for something other than crops or date-palms. He عليه السلام said: "He should specify a known measure up to a known term."
He said: And I asked him about salam in animals and food, and whether a man may take collateral for his money as a pledge. He عليه السلام said: "Yes, secure your wealth properly."

key_terms.أَجَلٍ مَعْلُومٍ: a fixed and known delivery term
key_terms.اسْتَوْثِقْ: take proper security or ensure protection
key_terms.الطَّعَامِ: food goods as the subject of sale
key_terms.الْحَيَوَانِ: livestock or animals as the subject of sale
key_terms.رَهْنًا: collateral or pledge taken as security
key_terms.كَيْلًا مَعْلُومًا: a specified known measure of the item being contracted
key_terms.يُسْلِمُ: enters into a salam contract or forward sale

ai.seo_question: Is a salam contract valid for animals or other goods, and can collateral be taken for it?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on salam transactions, permitting them beyond crops and dates so long as the quantity and delivery term are clearly specified. It also permits taking collateral in such dealings in order to safeguard one's property.
